home.intro: Nice to meet you, I'm Ágatha! The designer from your neighborhood, your multinational company and your cute indie game. I work with research (UX and UI), illustration and 3D Design.
home.philosophyLead: For me, design is research, illustration and perspective.
home.philosophyBody1: I believe design translates how I see the world and how I'd like to shape it, with an open heart to the people, cultures and stories I come across.
home.philosophyBody2End: as extensions of one purpose: listening to realities that aren't mine and turning them into especially sensitive experiences and worlds.
home.philosophyColUxEnd: brings me closer to other people's lived experience and turns research into a moment of listening and sharing, where we discover things together.
home.philosophyCol3dEnd: , I tell what I've heard in tiny scenes, the kind that make you stop to watch a ladybug climb a leaf.
home.experienceLead: The future lies in human activity, and it is what makes our experiences so important.

pontosSemNo.title: Pontos sem nó
pontosSemNo.subtitle: Brand Identity: Pontos sem nó
pontosSemNo.description: The “Pontos sem nó” brand seeks to transport us to the space between the lines of our deepest unresolved questions that always return to our minds in some way, converting memories into recognizable feelings… (PLACEHOLDER)
pontosSemNo.intro:
The “Pontos sem nó” brand seeks to transport us to the space between the lines of our deepest unresolved questions that always return to our minds in some way, converting memories into recognizable feelings. Pontos sem nó seeks to be part of the moment of identification, conveying the process of acceptance of those feelings in the form of music.

Represented through lines of tenderness, serenity with a lyrical touch that makes us take on the role of a pilgrim in other dimensions through escapism.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The beginning of the process was marked by guided research, building a semantic board to orient the conceptual decisions of the project. After the research, selections of elements, typefaces, colors and other representations were made to enrich the brand's conceptual repertoire and make its application easier.

batucoTuco.title: Batuco-tuco
batucoTuco.subtitle: Batuco-tuco App
batucoTuco.description: Batuco-Tuco is a mobile application focused on the gamification of music theory and instrument practice. Its name alludes to the “batuque” and pays tribute to a Brazilian species and its sound, the tuco-tuco… (PLACEHOLDER)
batucoTuco.intro:
Batuco-Tuco is a mobile application focused on the gamification of music theory and instrument practice. Its name alludes to the “batuque” and pays tribute to a Brazilian species and its sound, the tuco-tuco, inspiring the playful theme and visual style of the project, which turns animals into skilled musicians.

The project was developed as a hands-on study of graphical interfaces and UX/UI. To ensure a smooth evolution with real-time visual feedback, the process involved structuring content maps, building a design system and applying user-centered methodologies.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: Developed in the Graphical Interface Design course (Unifor), the challenge was to create a scalable Design System and cohesive usability flows. I prioritized basic requirements, such as the practice activities, to guarantee functionality before moving on to complex band interactions. In three weeks, I finished the entire interface, assets and animations, focusing on prototyping optimization.

identidadeEvento15Anos.title: Event identity: 15th birthday
identidadeEvento15Anos.subtitle: Event identity: 15th birthday
identidadeEvento15Anos.description: Illustrated visual identity for a pair of twins' 15th birthday, from the save the date to the applications on the day of the event.
identidadeEvento15Anos.intro: The commission called for a visual identity for the 15th birthday party of a pair of twins. The service was planned around a delivery schedule, to keep the client quickly updated on the process and to show her how my work was expected to unfold.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The process was split into defining the scope with the client, building a moodboard of visual references, defining the text content, sketching and prototyping. From the answers to my general briefing form for service requests, the production scope was set, giving the pieces the following characteristics: minimalist and elegant, delicate and organic, favoring pink, yellow and green, with flowers as the main elements. A moderate, stylized level of detail, intended for promotion in digital and print media.
images: First reference board: watercolor floral invitations, botanical stickers, yellow flowers and delicate frames.
Second reference board: paintings of gardens and landscapes with flowers in shades of green, orange and pink.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: The process started with the “Save the date”, which would also give structure to the invitation and the pieces that followed. But input from more people shifted the project's vision a little, adding new references and changing the complexity of the illustration. The main illustration guided the composition of further pieces, such as party favor tags, menus, cake box stickers and even the wrap of a “mini cakes” favor cart hired by the client. After testing the prints and making the necessary revisions, the material was applied to the promotion and to the printed surfaces. Every step was approved by the client.

cascavel.title: City of Cascavel
cascavel.subtitle: City of Cascavel
cascavel.description: A VR project that playfully explores the legend of the serpent-like creature living beneath the soil of Cascavel, CE.
cascavel.intro:
“Cascavel” is a VR (virtual reality) project that playfully and light-heartedly explores the legend of a huge creature living beneath the soil of the city of Cascavel, CE. With the appearance of a serpent, the creature grows every time its name is spoken in the city, until its den erupts and it has a catastrophic encounter with the city's population. The brief called for an experience only a few minutes long, part of the opening exhibition “Edson e Yolanda” at the new Cultural Complex of the University of Fortaleza. The idea was for the experience to evoke memories of the city's characteristics and for the story to have fun and unusual endings, while keeping the interaction accessible and immersive for family audiences.

From this proposal, I was responsible for scripting the experience and its flow map, sketching, modeling and refining the stylized low-poly 3D map, creating custom assets and adapting previously selected models, animating some characters, creating textures, composing scenarios and modeling the Cascavel itself in two versions.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The creation and development process was carried out together with my coworkers Amanda, Raquel and Felipe. At first, we read cordel literature about the city available at the University of Fortaleza library, looked for references of tourist spots and landmark spaces in the city, and from that I wrote a script and listed the elements that would compose the environment. After setting dates for the production stages of each element, I began creating the models, and the following stages were refining the map, making small animations and testing the experience with potential users.
images: Flow map of the VR experience, with the scenes, timings and player choices (Start → End)

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: The initial map structure was built from an assembly of free-license models. My role was to compose the scenario, adding the previously planned elements so that its buildings and spaces felt more alive, always making sure there were fewer polygons and that the scenario optimization was efficient. Besides that model, specific elements were created or adapted by me throughout the production (Image A) for the city's context, such as the grotto, the downtown chapel, the cajuzinho market, the bandstand, the bodega, small street markets and little playgrounds. The choice of colors and shaders was also intentional, as they tell about the everyday life and the extravagant simplicity of living in Cascavel.

I also created designs tied to spaces often recognized as “from the Ceará countryside” and textures for specific moments (Image B), such as the painting of the Cascavel made by the children that the player sees at the little school.
